          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.8 active sessions, 15.54% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.8 active sessions, 15.54% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Top SQL Statements
Impact is 1.62 active sessions, 13.94% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .6 active sessions, 5.18% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "8as8s1k2fhhqb" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.09 active sessions, 9.4% of total activity.

      disconnects.

      analysis period.

Finding 2: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.56 active sessions, 13.7% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.56 active sessions, 13.7% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 3: Soft Parse
Impact is .87 active sessions, 7.66% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .87 active sessions, 7.66% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .87 active sessions, 7.66% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "300" during the
      analysis period.

additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

      Impact is .83 active sessions, 7.32% of total activity.

were consuming significant database time.

Finding 8: Undersized SGA
Impact is .12 active sessions, 1.06% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "184320 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .02 active sessions, .22% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      207360 M.

   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .83 active sessions, 7.32% of total activity.
      Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .33 active sessions, 2.86% of total activity.

Finding 3: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.19 active sessions, 10.62% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.19 active sessions, 10.62% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.19 active sessions, 10.62% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "300" during the
      analysis period.

Finding 6: Undersized SGA
Impact is .5 active sessions, 4.44% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "184320 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .48 active sessions, 4.27% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      299520 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .88 active sessions, 7.86% of total activity.


Finding 7: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .47 active sessions, 4.16% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .47 active sessions, 4.16% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .88 active sessions, 7.86% of total activity.


Finding 8: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is .43 active sessions, 3.82% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .43 active sessions, 3.82% of total activity.

      online redo log files.

      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and
